A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BioDiscoveryAgent. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support comparison; renamed datasets and relocated analyses can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrospective closed-loop experiments on single-gene and gene-pair perturbation datasets, including baseline comparisons and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds evaluations across language models, tool configurations, and prediction-overlap analyses.

M1.justification: The gene-search component expands substantially from feature-based similarity/dissimilarity to expression-, tissue-, and pathway-based retrieval, with Reactome enrichment becoming the principal approach (Section 3.1, Appendix D). The overall prompting, feedback, and critic pipeline remains unchanged, including Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: The perturbation benchmarks and biological tasks remain unchanged; Steinhart is renamed CAR-T, and six evaluation columns already existed in v1. v2 adds ARCHS4 expression/tissue data and KEGG/Reactome pathways as information sources in evaluated retrieval variants (Appendix D, Table 5), modestly expanding supporting data coverage.

E2.justification: The same random, GeneDisco, and DiscoBax comparators remain in the single-gene comparisons, and random sampling remains the gene-pair comparator. The additional language models are configurations of BioDiscoveryAgent rather than new external baselines.

E3.justification: Evaluation expands from Claude v1 to nine language-model configurations. The new Sonnet observation ablation measures between-run Jaccard similarity after 30 rounds, while the original 10-round comparison remains in the appendix. Appendix D also changes the stated dissimilar-search retrieval count from 50 to 10. Core benchmark budgets and hit-ratio evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1's individual-tool Claude v1 ablations are replaced by Haiku/Sonnet analyses, broader comparisons of tool effects across models, and six gene-search variants. New Figure 7 examines overlap between tool-assisted and unaided predictions. A Sonnet observation ablation supplements the original Claude v1 analysis, retained as Figure 8 and Table 9.

E5.justification: Most benchmarks retain ten-run, one-standard-deviation reporting. The new main observation ablation uses eight runs, while the original ten-run analysis remains in the appendix. Standard deviations previously reported for Claude v1 All-Tools in v1 Table 5 are absent from the corresponding v2 Table 8 entries.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive model and tool results. Table 2 replaces the original agent's 32.67 round-five hits with 45.1 for Haiku and 40.0 for Sonnet 3.5; these use different backbones. Tool results now include substantial negative effects. Some overlapping entries conflict: v2 Table 6 reports Claude v1/Sanchez as 0.058, while Table 1 retains v1's 0.053.

T1.justification: New Figure 7 defines a set-overlap fraction measuring how many tool-added Haiku predictions appear in unaided Sonnet predictions. The single-gene and gene-pair formulations and hit-ratio definition remain unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains interpretable closed-loop experiment design without task-specific model training or an explicit acquisition function. The abstract and introduction now anchor performance claims to Claude 3.5 Sonnet, reporting 21% and 46% improvements instead of 18% and 29%, and describe gene-pair performance as more than twice random.

C2.justification: v1 presents All-Tools as consistently advantageous. v2 substantially qualifies this interpretation: tools benefit some backbones but hurt others. It introduces the hypothesis that larger models already contain information supplied by tools, using token price as a size proxy and prediction overlap as supporting evidence. Existing cell-type and early-round limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix D adds feature provenance and database-specific retrieval details. Model identities and token prices are documented, and a new reproducibility statement specifies prompt/data distribution and offers anonymized CAR-T data upon request. The code link, prompts, pseudocode, and complete agent trace are retained.

R1.justification: Related work adds biological benchmarks and explicitly distinguishes BioDiscoveryAgent's iterative hypothesis selection from CRISPR-GPT's individual experiment design. Additional citations document newer models, biological databases, and scientific agents. The original positioning around closed-loop biological experiment design remains.

P1.justification: The seven main sections and appendices A-F remain, with much prose and the complete trace preserved. Changes include focused results rewrites and reordering, expanded tool explanations, updated authorship and terminology, and new ethics and reproducibility statements.

P2.justification: Table 1 combines all-gene and non-essential results and introduces grouped model rows. Tool tables gain model panels and percentage annotations, and new cost and retrieval comparisons are added. The workflow and original observation figure move to the appendix, while new observation and overlap figures appear. Document typography and layout also change.

improvement.justification: The broader model evaluation strengthens evidence beyond Claude v1 and replaces a broadly positive tool-use conclusion with useful model-dependent findings. The net gain is limited by reporting problems: v2 Tables 1 and 6 disagree on Claude v1/Sanchez, and Figure 3 does not support the text's claimed late-round advantage of Observation Only over Prompt Only. The proposed model-size explanation also remains tentative.
